title: Mamajek and colleagues: best-estimate mean solar luminosity is 3.8275 (±0.0014) × 10^26 W
summary: Using the exact astronomical unit and the TSI best estimate, the paper calculates a mean solar luminosity of 3.8275 (±0.0014) × 10^26 W, beside a nominal value of 3.828 × 10^26 W.
body: Endnote 4 says IAU 2012 Resolution B2 defined the astronomical unit as exactly 149 597 870 700 m. Using that length and the TSI best estimate, the paper states a current best estimate of the Sun's mean radiative luminosity L = 4 π (1 au)^2 S = 3.8275 (±0.0014) × 10^26 W. The nominal luminosity in the resolution table is 3.828 × 10^26 W, described as the mean radiative luminosity rounded to an appropriate number of significant figures. The 3.8275 figure is a calculation from a measured irradiance and an exact length. The 3.828 figure is the rounded nominal constant. Endnote 2 says Haberreiter and colleagues (2008) determined the photospheric radius, where the Rosseland optical depth is 2/3, to be 695 658 (±140) km, and that the nominal radius 6.957 × 10^8 m is that value quoted to fewer figures. Endnote 5 says the best-estimate effective temperature calculated from those luminosity and radius estimates and the CODATA 2014 Stefan-Boltzmann constant is 5772.0 (±0.8) K. The nominal effective temperature is 5772 K.
